chapter: Trent's band: Texas, St. Louis and the road east
title: Songs: Sunshine Sammy, Blue Memories and Substitute for Love
summary: He wrote a piece first titled Sunshine Sammy, later renamed; Blue Memories was published with Mills; a Decca recording followed.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: This is where this song was written?
I wrote that just about this time, but you know the name of this song, what it was given at first?
What?
Sunshine Sammy.
Sunshine Sammy?
That's it.
You see, he was a child star and he was the only--I'd say he was about the only one, the only black person.
Yeah; that was a big deal at that time.
Sunshine Sammy (singing).
That was the name of the piece. I later changed it to You're the Kisses.
Were you using this as a theme song?
We used another number on that--Blue Memories.
Were you that far back? That was never published, was it?
I published Blue Memories with Mills a year later--way, way later.
Do they have it?
They've got it now.
Did they ever print it?
Oh, yes.
Do you have copies?
Yes, I've got one copy.
You should bring it down and let me see it; I never saw it.
Here's another--
That's later. I got something called I'm Just a Substitute for Love.
You got a record of that?
No, not a record. I think I have the sheet music somewhere.
Yeah; I got it too. I'm Just a Substitute for Love; I'd like to get a record on that.
Did you ever make a record of that?
I made a Decca record of it.
